column3: The Hebrew says the king placed Haman’s throne above all the princes; BSB describes elevation to a position above them.
The Hebrew asks whether Mordecai’s words would stand; BSB asks whether his behavior would be tolerated.
The Hebrew says they told him Mordecai’s people and uses a singular hand in describing the action he scorned; BSB omits the informants and uses hands in the plural.
The Hebrew runs from day to day and from month to month to the twelfth month without a separate statement that the lot fell; BSB supplies that statement.
The Hebrew promises to weigh silver into the hands of those doing the work to bring it into the king’s treasuries; BSB describes depositing it in the treasury to pay those carrying it out.
The Hebrew names his hand; BSB specifies his finger.
The Hebrew says the silver is given to Haman; BSB renders this as an instruction to keep his money.
